items.title: ‘We’re Done’: MGM Resorts Ends Merger Talks With Barry Diller’s People Inc.
items.summary: A new pact between MGM Resorts and Barry Diller's People Inc. effectively ends merger talks. It's uncertain who else might want to buy an operator whose Las Vegas resorts have been sliding for two years.

items.title: Vrbo Launches Reserve Now, Pay Later — With a Twist on Airbnb’s Approach
items.summary: Paying nothing up-front has been one of Airbnb's clearest growth levers. Vrbo's version of Reserve Now, Pay Later seems more host-friendly, but it gives guests less flexibility in when they can cancel without penalty. Will that weaken the tailwinds for Vrbo that Airbnb

items.title: Marriott Confirms Corporate Job Cuts
items.summary: Marriott is cutting corporate jobs, not hotel staff, in a global restructuring. Some affected workers may land newly posted roles, it says.

items.title: Frontier’s Fares Soar, But Spirit’s Exit Hasn’t Fixed Its Profit Problem
items.summary: Spirit's collapse has given Frontier room to raise fares and attract more passengers – but record revenues have yet to translate into meaningful profits.

items.title: Why Luxury Escapes Puts Its Best Prices Behind a Paywall
items.summary: Travel customers switch platforms on price and inventory with little friction, and Luxury Escapes’ CEO builds around that. His bet is a paid membership with a genuine paywall over partner pricing, a moat he expects to matter more as AI agents enter booking.

items.title: The New Math Behind Travel’s AI Roll-Ups
items.summary: AI could give travel consolidators a new way to improve the companies they buy. The question is whether the gains are real, repeatable, and worth the price of admission.

items.title: Airbnb.org Aims for 1 Million Free Nights a Year, Funded Partly by a Dime a Booking
items.summary: Is 10 cents per booking enough of a contribution? Well, it's more than Booking.com and Vrbo donate per stay.

items.title: Waymo Picks Ramp for Its First Business Travel Expense Partner: Exclusive
items.summary: Waymo’s receipts will now flow straight into a spend platform used by more than 70,000 businesses. That should fix a pain point for road warriors, and it’s a signal that Waymo wants a bigger slice of corporate travel.
